learning_outcomes.text: Knows the theory of biosolids and biofluid mechanics.
Learns to model and analyze a current biomechanics problem using open-source modern software tools.
Has the ability to apply relevant mathematical theories and numerical solutions.
Can deliver the obtained information in explanatory technical reports and presentations.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to biomechanic: Definitions, axis, planes, biological structures etc.
Anatomy: Parts of the human body, bones, muscles and circulation systems.
Viscoelastisity : Kelvin ve Maxwell models, generalized models.
Biofluid mechanic: Basic definitions and viscosity.
Biofluid mechanic: Continuty equation and momentum equation.
Biofluid mechanic: Fully developed laminar flow.
Lagrange dynamic: Equation of motion, generalized coordinates, Lagrange equations.
3D kinematics of linkages: Position analysis and transformation matrix.
bibliography: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics, R.W. Fox & A.T. McDonald, John 4. Wiley&Sons, Fourth Edition, 1994.
Theory and Problems of Continuum Mechanics, G.E. Mase, McGraw-Hill, 1970.
Biomechanics: Motion, Flow, Stress and Growth, Y.C. Fung, Springer-Verlag, 1990.
Advanced Strength and Applied Elasticity, A.C. Ugural & S.K. Fenster, Prentice Hall, Third Edition, 1995.
Theory of Machines and Mechanisms, J. E Shigley & J. J. Uicker, McGraw-Hill, Second Edition, 1995.
Biomechanics: Mechanical Properties of Living Tissues, 2.Edition, Y.C. Fung, Springer-Verlag, 1993.
